menu_option_descriptions.ptvo_mqtt: A PTVO firmware Zigbee device bridges the heater's RS232 port, zigbee2mqtt publishes it on MQTT.
menu_option_descriptions.serial: The heater's RS232 port is connected to the Home Assistant host, e.g. with a USB serial adapter.

data_description.topic: Base topic of the PTVO device in zigbee2mqtt, without /set.
data_description.broker: Use the broker of Home Assistant's MQTT integration or a different one.

data_description.host: Hostname or IP address of the MQTT broker zigbee2mqtt publishes to.
data_description.username: Leave empty if the broker allows anonymous access.

data_description.device: Prefer a /dev/serial/by-id/ path, it does not change when devices are plugged in.
data_description.baudrate: The heater uses 19200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit.

levels.title: Monitor list levels
levels.description: Choose the levels of the heater's monitor list. After this step the list is read from the heater once, which can take several minutes, especially over Zigbee. Values of deeper levels are created disabled and can be enabled one by one.

data_description.levels: Levels 0 to 3. Deeper levels add more values.

error.mqtt_not_available: The MQTT integration is not set up. Set it up first or use an external broker.
error.no_response: Connected, but the heater did not answer.

data_description.levels: Levels 0 to 3 of the heater's monitor list. A change only takes effect when you press Read monitor list again on the device, because reading the list takes several minutes.
data_description.scan_interval: How often the enabled values are read from the heater. The diagnostic sensor Read duration shows how long one read takes; disabling entities you do not need makes it shorter.
data_description.publish_errors: Also publish error messages as JSON to the zigbee2mqtt topic followed by /error, like the former AppDaemon app.
data_description.allow_commands: Adds buttons to switch the boiler on and off and to load hot water now, sent like the SMS commands of ETA's GSM connector. Commands for heating circuits only act on circuits with "SMS erlauben" set to yes; they are created disabled.

mqtt_not_available.message: The MQTT integration is not available

update_failed.message: Reading values from the heater failed: {error}

no_values.message: The heater did not send any values

reread_in_progress.message: The monitor list is already being read

busy_reading_list.message: The monitor list is being read, try again when it is done

nothing_to_acknowledge.message: Nothing to acknowledge, the display shows: {display}

levels_changed.title: Monitor list levels changed for {title}
levels_changed.description: The levels were changed to {levels}, but the values in use were read with levels {list_levels}. Press **Read monitor list again** on the device to read the list with the new levels. This takes several minutes; the current values stay available meanwhile.

monitor_list_failed.title: Monitor list of {title} could not be read
monitor_list_failed.description:
Reading the monitor list from the heater failed: {error}

Check the connection to the heater, then press **Read monitor list again** on the device.

other_program.title: Another program is talking to {title}
other_program.description:
The heater sends values that this integration did not request, so another program is communicating with the controller at the same time, for example the former AppDaemon app `eta2hass`. The controller cannot serve both: requests of this integration fail and reading the monitor list does not complete.

Stop the other program. In Home Assistant OS, disabling *Start on boot* does not stop an app that is running; use **Stop** on its page, and disable the app in AppDaemon's `apps.yaml` (`disable: true`). This notice disappears after the next read without foreign values.
